## Claims
- [source-backed] \(\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}\) has Schur \(\mathbb Z\)-basis, \(I_{r,q}\) is the ideal spanned by \(s_\lambda\) with \(\lambda\nsubseteq q^r\), and \(\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) has basis indexed by \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\). [source-2, lines 1312-1330]
- [source-backed] For \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(J_v\subseteq\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) is generated by \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). [source-2, lines 1365-1375]
- [source-backed] The 2024 Theorem 1.2 applies to admissible bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), with \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), and proves minimality of \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 95-110]
- [proved] The Schur transposition map \(\omega:\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}\to\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}\), \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\), is an integral ring involution and descends to an integral ring isomorphism
  \[
  \omega_{r,q}:\Lambda/I_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda/I_{q,r}.
  \]
- [proved] For \(q=n-r\), \(\omega_{r,q}(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}})=J_{v'}\), where
  \[
  v'=v_{\,q,\ q-i+j,\ q-i+1,\ n},
  \qquad (i',j',a',b')=(j,i,a,b).
  \]
- [proved] The transposed family
  \[
  \mathcal T=\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}
  \]
  maps under \(\omega_{r,q}\) to
  \[
  \omega_{r,q}(\mathcal T)
  =\{\bar s_\nu:j^i\subseteq\nu\subseteq(j^i,b^a)\},
  \]
  precisely the family covered by 2024 Theorem 1.2 for \(v'\). Consequently \(\mathcal T\) is minimal whenever that theorem is invoked for \(v'\). The requested transpose-involution reduction is established.

## Strategy
Put \(q=n-r\). Define \(\omega(h_k)=e_k\). The identities
\[
\sum_{k\ge0}h_kz^k\sum_{k\ge0}(-1)^ke_kz^k=1
\]
show that this is an integral involution; Jacobi--Trudi gives
\(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\).

Since
\[
\lambda\nsubseteq q^r\iff\lambda'\nsubseteq r^q,
\]
one has \(\omega(I_{r,q})=I_{q,r}\), proving the asserted quotient isomorphism over \(\mathbb Z\), without localization.

For admissible \(v_{r,s,t,n}\),
\[
i=s-t+1,\quad j=r-t+1,\quad
a=\min(q-i,r-j),\quad b=\min(i,j).
\]
The hypotheses
\[
1\le t\le r,s\le n,\qquad t>r+s-n
\]
imply \(i\le q\) and \(j\le r\). Hence
\[
r'=q,\quad t'=q-i+1,\quad s'=q-i+j
\]
satisfy
\[
1\le t'\le r',s'\le n,\qquad t'>r'+s'-n.
\]
Moreover,
\[
i'=s'-t'+1=j,\quad j'=r'-t'+1=i,
\]
and
\[
a'=\min(n-r'-i',r'-j')=\min(r-j,q-i)=a,\qquad b'=b.
\]

Conjugation preserves Young-diagram inclusion, so the source-backed Schur description of \(J_v\) yields
\[
\omega_{r,q}(J_v)
=\left\langle\bar s_\nu:j^i\subseteq\nu\subseteq r^q\right\rangle
=J_{v'}.
\]
Finally,
\[
\bigl((i+a)^b,i^{j-b}\bigr)'
=(j^i,b^a).
\]
Thus \(\omega_{r,q}(\mathcal T)\) is the theorem’s family for \(v'\). Ring isomorphisms preserve generation and the property that no member of a finite generating family can be removed; applying \(\omega_{r,q}^{-1}\) transfers Theorem 1.2’s minimality to \(\mathcal T\).

## Gaps
None for this reduction, relative to the cited 2024 Theorem 1.2.
